requirement.clarified: Replace the trip editor's rendering engine with the React template used by generate-html-interactive.py. Serve the React-generated HTML from serve-trip.py for GET /trip/<id>, inject EDITOR_MODE=true, and add CandidatesSidebar + drag-and-drop + selection state as React components on top. Visual parity with the published page is guaranteed by sharing the same React component tree.
requirement.what: Architectural replacement: serve-trip.py generates React HTML (same template as published page) with editor-only components (CandidatesSidebar, slot drop zones, selection state bridge) added via editorMode flag in react_template.tpl
requirement.why: Four previous CSS-patching attempts failed because the editor and published page have structurally different component trees. Visual parity can only be achieved by sharing the same rendering engine.

root_cause_analysis.symptom: The trip editor at /trip/<id> looks completely different from the published static page: wrong font (Inter vs ui-sans-serif), wrong cover mechanism (img vs background-div), wrong card dimensions, wrong layout (3-panel vanilla HTML vs React flex).
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: The editor (web/index.html + web/js/state.js) and the published page (react_template.tpl) are two entirely separate applications. The editor was built from scratch using vanilla JS and CSS instead of extending the existing React template. No CSS adjustment can bridge structurally different component trees.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — accumulated architectural divergence across multiple cycles
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The editor was built as a new application focused on drag-and-drop interactivity, without reusing the existing React template as a base.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: All CSS-patching attempts (4 prior cycles) are symptoms-only fixes that cannot achieve visual parity because the HTML structure is fundamentally different.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Architectural divergence introduced during M4a spec (spec-20260508-221237). Patching attempts over 4+ subsequent cycles.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex confirmed: (1) vanilla JS injection into React DOM is unsound — React-side changes required; (2) exchange rate subprocess is a per-request blocker — cache required; (3) state.js cannot be injected wholesale; (4) candidates sidebar must be a React component inside the root flex layout; (5) interaction model must be named-slot (drag sets selected_option_id for a specific slot); (6) drag.js must be refactored to be framework-neutral; (7) window bridge (window.setEditorSelection) required for React re-render; (8) editorMode flag is the correct minimal change pattern; (9) hyphenated filename requires importlib; (10) live browser verification ACs required.

findings.issue: Approach A (inject vanilla JS on top) is not sound — React owns the DOM under #root
findings.proposed_fix: Reuse generated React template as editor shell; render candidates, drop zones, and selection state through React; vanilla drag code may only dispatch events into React
findings.rationale: Architecture revised: CandidatesSidebar is a React component inside NotionTravelApp, not an external panel

findings.issue: Per-request InteractiveHTMLGenerator blocks HTTP up to 10s via exchange rate subprocess
findings.proposed_fix: Keep GET /trip/<id> on fast path via in-memory HTML cache; never run exchange rate subprocess during editor page load
findings.rationale: Cache strategy added to serve-trip.py requirements and Technical Hints

findings.issue: Cache invalidation must be tied to persisted saves, not just request-time memory
findings.proposed_fix: On successful save, invalidate HTML cache for that trip_id
findings.rationale: Invalidation on save success added to cache design

findings.issue: state.js cannot be injected into React page — auto-init fails on missing DOM IDs
findings.proposed_fix: Treat state.js as reference logic only; implement equivalent mutation flow in React
findings.rationale: state.js explicitly excluded from scope; window.setEditorSelection bridge specified instead

findings.issue: Candidates sidebar must be a React component inside NotionTravelApp, not an injected vanilla panel
findings.proposed_fix: Add <CandidatesSidebar /> inside root flex layout with correct data attributes
findings.rationale: CandidatesSidebar specified as React component in react_template.tpl

findings.issue: Interaction model unspecified — must clarify named-slot semantics
findings.proposed_fix: Users drag candidate into named active-day slot; drop sets selected_option_id for that slot
findings.rationale: Named slot interaction model specified in requirements and AC5

findings.issue: KanbanView has no drop zones — underspecified where drops land
findings.proposed_fix: Either keep KanbanView read-only with drop zones in TimelineView, or add explicit slot-drop zones per category section header in KanbanView
findings.rationale: Option A (drop zones in category headers) recommended; dev may choose Option B

findings.issue: editorMode flag is the minimal safe change pattern
findings.proposed_fix: Add EDITOR_MODE defaulting false; when true render CandidatesSidebar and slot-drop zones; existing KanbanView styles unchanged
findings.rationale: editorMode/EDITOR_MODE flag specified in render_html_builders.py and react_template.tpl requirements

findings.issue: window global does not trigger React re-render
findings.proposed_fix: Expose window.setEditorSelection(dayN, slotId, optionId) inside useEffect that calls setState
findings.rationale: window.setEditorSelection bridge specified in requirements and Technical Hints

findings.issue: drag.js imports state.js/mobile.js — pulls in vanilla auto-init path
findings.proposed_fix: Refactor drag.js to accept callbacks as parameters; no imports from state.js or mobile.js
findings.rationale: drag.js refactor specified as Must Have S2

findings.issue: generate-html-interactive.py not importable due to hyphenated filename
findings.proposed_fix: Use importlib.util.spec_from_file_location() or move class to scripts/lib/html_generator.py
findings.rationale: importlib pattern included in Technical Hints; note to check html_generator.py first

findings.issue: Verification must include live browser rendering checks
findings.proposed_fix: ACs must require desktop and mobile browser checks with specific pixel measurements
findings.rationale: All 8 ACs specify measurable browser-observable outcomes

codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: All 12 Codex findings classified and applied. Architecture revised from vanilla-JS-injection to React-native approach. Exchange rate caching strategy added. drag.js refactor scoped. window bridge specified. All ACs include live browser verification requirements.
